chunks: Fear Allah, before Whom attendance is inevitable,
and with other than Whom there is no meeting.
Do not fight except with those who fight you.
Travel in the two cool periods,
Let the men have a midday sleep.
and do not travel during the early night,
for Allah has made it for resting,
and has ordained it for staying, not for journeying.
Therefore, give rest to your body in the night,
and let your carrier-beasts also rest.
When you are sure that morning has appeared and when dawn has dawned, commence your journey with Allah’s blessings.

key_terms.السَّحَرُ: The last part of the night before dawn
key_terms.الْبَرْدَيْنِ: The two cool periods (morning and evening)

ai.seo_question: What are the key principles of military conduct and travel etiquette in Shia Islam according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) frames military discipline within a cosmic order, urging soldiers to fight only in self-defense while adhering to the Sunnah of traveling during the cool hours and resting at night, thereby aligning human effort with divine wisdom. This guidance reflects the Shia emphasis on combining spiritual piety (Taqwa) with strategic pragmatism, ensuring that physical endurance supports spiritual readiness for the encounter with Allah.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Fear Allāh before Whom attendance is inevitable, and with other than Whom there is no meeting.
Do not fight except with those who fight you.
Travel in the two cool periods (i.e., morning and evening).
Let the men have a midday sleep.
and do not travel during the early night
for Allāh has made it for resting
and has ordained it for staying, not for journeying.
Therefore, give rest to your body in the night
and let your carrier-beasts also rest.
When you are sure that morning has appeared and when dawn has dawned, commence your journey with Allāh’s blessings.
